title: Camping by the lake
text:
Thursday 18 June

Dear Diary,

I did not want to go to school camp. I thought it would be cold, I would miss my own bed, and I would not know how to put up a tent. Now I think it was the best three days of my life, and today was only the first one!

We arrived at Lake Ullswater at eleven o'clock after a long coach journey. Mr Jenkins showed us how to pitch the tents. Ours kept falling down because Sam pulled the wrong rope. Eventually Priya worked out which pegs went where, and by lunchtime our tent was the straightest on the field.

In the afternoon we went kayaking. The lake was calm and flat, like a huge mirror, and the mountains were reflected in the water. I paddled so hard on the left side that I went round in circles, and everyone laughed, including me. A duck followed us all the way back to the shore, probably hoping for crumbs.

Tonight we cooked sausages over the fire. Mine was burnt black on the outside and cold in the middle, but I ate every bit of it. Later, Mr Jenkins pointed out the Plough, a pattern of seven stars that looks like a saucepan. Priya said it looked more like a kite to her. I could see why.

It is nearly lights out, and I can hear an owl hooting nearby. I am so tired that my pen keeps slipping. I wonder what tomorrow will bring.

Goodnight,
Tom
